5. Adjustments with no name on them. → Every change has a name and a time.

Phantom stock isn't theft most of the time. It's small gaps in logging.

content.Title: Calculate what an empty shelf costs you
content.Headline (EN): What does an empty shelf cost you?
content.Support line (EN): Do the maths with your own numbers.
content.On-image elements (HTML layer): Cover OB-37; formula slides with blank boxes to fill.
content.Slides (carousels):
1. What does an empty shelf cost you?
2. Sales lost per day × days out of stock.
3. × your margin on that item.
4. + the customers who buy elsewhere next time.
5. = the real cost. Usually more than the stock itself.
6. Comment COST and we'll send you the calculator.
content.Caption (EN):
No industry averages. Your numbers, your answer.
Comment COST and we'll DM you a simple calculator sheet.
